title: Paid for with a gradient: membrane transport

objectives.statement: Classify a named crossing of a membrane as simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion, primary active transport, or secondary active transport by applying a two-part test to the conditions stated, justify the classification from that test rather than from the identity of the protein involved, and name a case that sits on the category boundary instead of presenting the boundary as clean.

Compute the free-energy change for one mole of sodium entering an absorptive cell from a stated concentration ratio and membrane potential, keeping both the chemical and the electrical term, convert the coupled budget into the largest glucose concentration ratio the transporter could sustain, treat the coupling stoichiometry as the exponent it is rather than as a multiplier, and state what the resulting figure does not determine.

Explain why a cotransporter that hydrolyses no ATP nevertheless fails once ATP is withdrawn, trace the chain from ATP hydrolysis by one protein through an ion gradient to the coupled step performed by another, identify the observation that distinguishes indirect from direct dependence, and state the limit of what that observation can establish.
